kurz: How the statutory pension is financed on a pay-as-you-go basis and calculated from four factors, and how to read the figures in the annual pension statement.

bloecke.md:
The statutory pension insurance does not build up capital. What is paid in during September has already been paid out by October. In 2025, it took in around €422.6 billion and spent around €426.5 billion, of which €379.4 billion went on pensions for about 21.5 million people. The difference was covered from the sustainability reserve (Nachhaltigkeitsrücklage), a reserve of little more than one month's expenditure.

There is no individual account in which contributions paid in are held and earn interest. With their contributions, insured persons acquire an entitlement. They collect [[Earnings point (Entgeltpunkt)|earnings points (Entgeltpunkte)]], and these points determine their share of future pay-as-you-go revenue. This principle is called the intergenerational contract (Generationenvertrag). Today's contributors finance today's pensions and in return acquire an entitlement against tomorrow's contributors. The intergenerational contract is not set down in writing anywhere. It applies for as long as the legislature upholds it.

bloecke.titel: Pension insurance revenue in 2025 by source
bloecke.unter: Around a quarter of revenue comes from the federal budget, so contributions alone have long been far from sufficient to finance the system.

teile.name: Contributions from insured persons and employers

bloecke.md: The contributions are not invested; they are paid out immediately as pensions. Instead of capital, insured persons acquire a share, measured in earnings points, of what future contributors and the federal budget provide.

## The earnings point

One earnings point is credited when someone earns exactly as much in a year as the average of all insured persons. For 2026, the Social Security Calculation Values Ordinance (Sozialversicherungs-Rechengrößenverordnung) sets these provisional average earnings at €51,944 a year. Earnings of exactly this amount yield 1.0 points, half of it yields 0.5 points and double it would in theory yield 2.0 points.

The 2.0 points are not reached, because there is a contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze). In 2026 it is €8,450 a month, that is, €101,400 a year. On income above it, no contributions are due and no points are credited. At most 101,400 / 51,944 = 1.95 earnings points can therefore be achieved in a year. The contribution rate has been unchanged at 18.6% since 2018, with employees and employers each bearing 9.3%.

The points for all years are added together. Periods of child-rearing, caregiving, unemployment and education also earn points or at least count towards the qualifying period (Wartezeit).

bloecke.formel: Monthly pension = Earnings points × Pension access factor × Pension type factor × Current pension value
bloecke.erklaerung: The pension formula under Section 64 SGB VI (Social Code Book VI, pension insurance) consists of exactly four factors. Earnings points, the pension access factor (Zugangsfaktor) and the pension type factor (Rentenartfaktor) depend on the individual insured person. Earnings points grow with every contribution year, the pension access factor results from the chosen start of the pension and the pension type factor from the type of pension. The current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert), by contrast, is set anew every year according to calculation rules and political decisions.
variablen: Sum over all years: your own gross pay subject to contributions divided by the average earnings of the year in question (Sections 63 and 70 SGB VI)
1.0 when the pension starts at the standard retirement age; minus 0.003 per month drawn early, plus 0.005 per month of deferral (Section 77 SGB VI)
1.0 for the old-age pension and full reduced earning capacity, 0.5 for partial reduced earning capacity, 0.55 for the large widow's pension (große Witwenrente, Section 67 SGB VI)
€42.52 since 1 July 2026, uniform nationwide, valid until 30 June 2027 (Section 68 SGB VI)

bloecke.md:
## The current pension value

The current pension value states how many euros of monthly pension one earnings point yields. It is adjusted every year on 1 July, mainly in line with wage growth, dampened by the contribution rate factor and the sustainability factor (Beitragssatzfaktor, Nachhaltigkeitsfaktor). On 1 July 2026 it rose by 4.24% from €40.79 to €42.52. Since 1 July 2023 there has no longer been a separate pension value for eastern Germany (Rentenwert Ost); the alignment is complete.

The time series shows that the value rises reliably in nominal terms, by around 3.5% a year over eleven years, but it can also stand still. In 2021 there was a zero adjustment (Nullrunde), because wages had fallen in the pandemic year and only a safeguard clause prevented a cut. What matters for purchasing power is the adjustment minus inflation. In the years of high inflation, the adjustment was below the inflation rate on several occasions.

bloecke.titel: Current pension value per earnings point, valid from 1 July of each year
bloecke.unter: In nominal terms, the pension value rose from €29.21 to €42.52 in eleven years, including one zero adjustment and several years below the inflation rate.

bloecke.md:
## A pension level of 48%

The **pre-tax safeguard level (Sicherungsniveau vor Steuern)**, colloquially called the pension level (Rentenniveau), is 48.0% in 2026. The figure is a ratio of two model quantities and does not describe a personal entitlement. It is the disposable standard pension after 45 years of average earnings divided by disposable average earnings. Disposable here means, on both sides, after deduction of social security contributions but before tax.

A simple comparison of the gross values gives a lower figure. The standard pension is 45 × 42.52 = €1,913.40. Average earnings of €51,944 correspond to €4,328.67 a month. This gives 1,913.40 / 4,328.67 = 44.2%. This value, too, assumes 45 uninterrupted years with exactly average earnings.

The 2025 pension package (Rentenpaket 2025) extended the 48% floor (Haltelinie) until 2031. In 2026, the pension value was set so that the level of 48% is reached exactly. What happens after 2031 is open.

bloecke.titel: Salary, earnings points and pension after 40 contribution years (illustrative calculation)

bloecke.md: As long as the salary is below the contribution assessment ceiling, the replacement ratio is the same for everyone, because in this range the statutory pension is strictly proportional to salary. Only above the ceiling does the ratio fall markedly. A salary of €150,000 yields the same pension as one of €101,400. High earners above the ceiling therefore have the largest relative gap.

- The pension level is not a personal percentage. It refers to the average earnings of all insured persons and not to your own final salary.
- The standard pension is not an average pension. The €1,913.40 is a calculation figure for 45 years at average earnings. The pensions actually paid out are, on average, considerably lower, especially after periods of part-time work or child-rearing.
- The gross pension is not disposable income. A gap measured against the gross pension is systematically too small.

bloecke.titel: Possible development of the contribution rate and the safeguard level (model calculation from the 2025 Pension Insurance Report)

bloecke.md:
## Start of the pension, reductions and supplements

The standard retirement age has been rising gradually since 2012 and is 67 for those born in 1964 or later. This cohort is the first to retire regularly at 67 and reaches the limit in 2031. For a regular pension start in 2026, the age limit is 66 years and 2 to 4 months. The minimum requirement for a pension entitlement is the [[Qualifying period (Wartezeit)|qualifying period]] of five years (Section 50 SGB VI).

There are two ways to retire earlier. The **old-age pension for long-term insured persons** (Altersrente für langjährig Versicherte, Section 36 SGB VI) requires 35 years of insurance and is possible from 63. For each month drawn early, a reduction of 0.3% applies, so 14.4% for four full years. The reduction is permanent, so it remains in place even after the standard retirement age has been reached, and it later also reduces the survivor's pension. The **old-age pension for particularly long-term insured persons** (Altersrente für besonders langjährig Versicherte, Section 38 SGB VI) requires a qualifying period of 45 years and is free of reductions, but for those born in 1964 or later it is only possible from 65.

A later start increases the pension. For every month that someone works beyond the standard retirement age without drawing the pension, there is a supplement of 0.5%. Since 1 January 2023, recipients of an old-age pension may earn additional income without limit.

bloecke.titel: Monthly pension from 40 earnings points at seven different starting ages (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: Only the pension access factor changes; additional earnings points from working longer are deliberately not taken into account. Between a pension start at 63 and one at 69 there is a difference of €449 a month for life.

bloecke.md: Periods of receiving unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld I) count towards the 45-year qualifying period, except in the last two years before the pension starts. In those two years, they only count if the benefit is due to the employer's insolvency or the complete closure of its business (Section 51(3a) SGB VI). Periods of citizen's income (Bürgergeld), called basic income support (Grundsicherungsgeld) since July 2026, do not count at all. Employees who become unemployed at 61 and firmly count on the full 45 years therefore regularly miss them by a narrow margin. They then receive only the pension after 35 years of insurance, with a permanent reduction of up to 14.4%. Insured persons who are close to the threshold should clarify their qualifying period with the pension insurance before any decision about ending their employment.

From the age of 50, you can make a compensatory payment under Section 187a SGB VI to offset a planned reduction in full or in part. The pension insurance calculates the amount on request (form V0210). The payment is deductible as a retirement provision expense under Section 10(1) no. 2 EStG (Income Tax Act). It increases the pension even if you end up working until the standard retirement age after all.

## Structure of the annual pension statement

Insured persons aged 27 or over with at least five years of contribution periods receive an annual pension statement (Renteninformation), and from 55 the more detailed pension report (Rentenauskunft) every three years (Section 109 SGB VI). The letter contains four figures that are often confused.

schritte.text: The pension that the earnings points already collected would produce at the standard retirement age, valued at today's pension value. It is the only figure that is not based on any assumptions.

schritte.titel: Pension for full reduced earning capacity
schritte.text: The pension that would be paid today if you could work less than three hours a day. For comparison, the average full reduced earning capacity pension in 2023 was around €1,059, and over 40% of applications were rejected.

A projection assuming that the average of the last five years continues unchanged until the standard retirement age. If part-time work, parental leave or a career jump falls within this period, the figure is distorted.
Nominal values in future euros. They look high but say nothing about purchasing power. For your own planning, you should calculate in today's euros throughout.

bloecke.md: The annual pension statement is only correct if the insurance account is complete. Periods of schooling, university, vocational training and time abroad are often missing. An application for pension account clarification (Kontenklärung, form V0100) closes these gaps. It should be made as early as possible, because evidence from thirty years ago is easier to obtain at fifty than at sixty-seven.

## Deductions from the gross pension

Pensioners with compulsory insurance bear only half of the health insurance contribution themselves. They pay 7.3% plus half of the additional contribution set by their health insurance fund, which averages 2.9% in 2026. The pensioner bears the long-term care insurance contribution of 3.6%, or 4.2% for childless people aged 23 and over, alone. Together, this comes to around 12.35%.

Income tax is then due. Pensions are subject to deferred taxation under the cohort principle (Kohortenprinzip, Section 22 no. 1 sentence 3 letter a EStG). The year in which the pension starts fixes the taxable portion for life; for a start in 2026 it is 84.0%. The remaining 16% is determined as a fixed amount in euros in the first full year of the pension and is not increased thereafter. Every later pension adjustment is therefore 100% taxable. Only pensions starting in 2058 will be taxed in full. In 2024, the Growth Opportunities Act (Wachstumschancengesetz) moved this end point back from 2040.

bloecke.titel: Standard pension before and after health and long-term care insurance (as of July 2026)
bloecke.unter: Around €236 goes on health and long-term care insurance; income tax is not yet taken into account.

bloecke.md: A standard pensioner pays income tax, albeit not much. Of an annual pension of €22,960.80, 84% is taxable, that is, €19,287. From this, the lump-sum allowance for income-related expenses (Werbungskosten-Pauschbetrag) of €102 is deducted, as are the health and long-term care contributions paid, which count as special expenses (Sonderausgaben), here just over €2,800. The remainder is above the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag) of around €12,348 (2026, single persons), so that a few hundred euros of income tax are due each year. If a company pension, rental income or capital income is added, this quickly becomes a four-digit amount.

bloecke.formel: Pension gap = Net requirement in retirement − (statutory pension after health insurance, care insurance and tax + other net entitlements)
bloecke.erklaerung: All four quantities are stated in today's purchasing power. This assumes that future pension adjustments offset inflation on average. In the past this was sometimes the case and sometimes not. For a cautious calculation, set the adjustment half a percentage point below expected inflation.
bloecke.beispiel: €2,200 requirement − €1,503 pension before tax = €697 gap a month

bloecke.md:
The example assumes a 45-year-old person with a gross salary of €4,000 a month (€48,000 a year) whose annual pension statement shows 20.0 earnings points. There are 22 years to go until the standard retirement age of 67.

1. Each year, 48,000 / 51,944 = 0.924 earnings points are added.
2. Up to 67, that makes 22 × 0.924 = 20.33 points, so 40.33 earnings points in total including the existing ones.
3. The gross pension is 40.33 × €42.52 = €1,714.83.
4. After deducting 12.35% for health and long-term care insurance, 1,714.83 × 0.8765 = €1,503.05 remains.
5. The requirement is assumed to be €2,200 a month in today's purchasing power.
6. The gap is 2,200 − 1,503 = €697 a month, that is, €8,364 a year.

Over 25 years of retirement, the gap adds up to just over €209,000 without interest. Income tax has not yet been deducted in step 4. In addition, the calculation assumes that the salary remains permanently in the same ratio to average earnings. If part-time work is planned, the years concerned should be calculated individually.

The 48% floor, which runs until 2031, is current law. The mothers' pension III (Mütterrente III) is also current law. From 1 January 2027, it recognises 36 instead of 30 months of child-rearing time for children born before 1992. That is around 0.5 earnings points or about €21 more monthly pension per child, which for technical reasons will only be paid from 2028, and then retroactively. Since 1 January 2026, the active pension (Aktivrente) under Section 3 no. 21 EStG has made up to €2,000 of wages a month tax-free if you continue working after the standard retirement age. Social security contributions are still due.

The recommendations of the Old-Age Security Commission (Alterssicherungskommission) are not yet law. On 23 June 2026, it presented thirty-three recommendations, including a statutory funded pension on the Swedish model with an additional contribution of 2%, shared equally by employers and employees, from around 2028. There is no law on this so far. The traffic-light coalition's earlier “generational capital” (Generationenkapital) never came into force.

mitnehmen: The statutory pension is an entitlement measured in earnings points and not a balance; its value depends on what future contributors and the federal budget provide.
The amount of the pension results from four factors: earnings points, pension access factor, pension type factor and current pension value (€42.52 since July 2026).
The pension level of 48% is a ratio of two model quantities and not a personal percentage; insured persons who earn above the contribution assessment ceiling have the largest relative gap.
Each month drawn early reduces the pension by 0.3%, each month deferred increases it by 0.5%, and both apply for life.
Calculate your own gap in today's euros and with the pension after health and long-term care insurance and tax, not with the gross figure from the annual pension statement.

begriffe.text: Unit of calculation for the statutory pension. A year with exactly the average earnings of all insured persons (€51,944 in 2026) yields 1.0 point. Because of the contribution assessment ceiling, at most around 1.95 points a year can be achieved.

The monthly pension in euros that one earnings point yields. Since 1 July 2026 it has been €42.52, uniform nationwide. It is adjusted every year on 1 July, mainly in line with wage growth (Section 68 SGB VI).

Factor in the pension formula for the time at which the pension starts. It is 1.0 at the standard retirement age, minus 0.003 for each month drawn early and plus 0.005 for each month deferred (Section 77 SGB VI). The effect lasts for life.

Ratio of the disposable standard pension after 45 years at average earnings to disposable average earnings, in each case after social security contributions and before tax. In 2026 it is 48.0%, secured until 2031 by the floor (Haltelinie). It is not a personal percentage of your last salary.

The part of the statutory pension that remains tax-free; for a pension starting in 2026 this is 16%. It is determined as a fixed amount in euros in the first full year of the pension and is not increased thereafter. Every later pension adjustment is therefore fully taxable (Section 22 EStG).

Minimum insurance period for a pension entitlement. It is five years for the standard old-age pension, 35 years for drawing the pension early from 63 with a reduction and 45 years for drawing it from 65 without a reduction (Sections 50, 36, 38 SGB VI).
